title: Cross-Modal Coupling Analysis with PhysioCrossModal
text: PhysioCrossModal provides comprehensive toolkit analyzing coupling synchrony physiological signals different modalities (e.g., EEG, EMG, ECG, EDA, MoCap). extends PhysioCore ecosystem : MultiPhysioExperiment container multi-modal recordings different sampling rates Spectral coherence (Welch multitaper methods) Phase synchrony measures (PLV, PLI, wPLI) Directed coupling (Granger causality) Time-domain coupling (cross-correlation, sliding-window) Wavelet time-frequency coherence PLV Statistical significance testing via surrogates bootstrap vignette walks complete cross-modal coupling analysis workflow.

title: Cross-Modal Coupling Analysis with PhysioCrossModal
text: PhysioCrossModal includes three data generators quick prototyping testing. start creating simulated EEG-EMG dataset corticomuscular coherence (CMC) 20 Hz.
code: library(PhysioCrossModal)  # Simulate EEG (500 Hz) and EMG (1000 Hz) with CMC at 20 Hz data <- make_eeg_emg(   n_sec = 10,   n_eeg_ch = 3,   n_emg_ch = 2,   sr_eeg = 500,   sr_emg = 1000,   cmc_freq = 20 )  pe_eeg <- data$eeg pe_emg <- data$emg

title: Cross-Modal Coupling Analysis with PhysioCrossModal

text: Putting together – minimal script analyzing EEG-EMG corticomuscular coherence:
code: library(PhysioCrossModal)  # 1. Create or load data data <- make_eeg_emg(n_sec = 10, sr_eeg = 500, sr_emg = 1000)  # 2. Wrap into MultiPhysioExperiment mpe <- MultiPhysioExperiment(EEG = data$eeg, EMG = data$emg)  # 3. Compute coherence matrix coh_mat <- coherenceMatrix(mpe,                             modality_x = "EEG", modality_y = "EMG",                             nperseg = 256L,                             freq_range = c(15, 25))  # 4. Test significance with FDR correction sig <- surrogateMatrixTest(mpe,                             modality_x = "EEG", modality_y = "EMG",                             method = "coherence",                             n_surrogates = 199,                             correction = "fdr",                             nperseg = 256L,                             freq_range = c(15, 25))  # 5. Detailed spectrum for the most coupled pair best <- which(sig$matrix == max(sig$matrix, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE) coh_detail <- coherence(mpe,                          modality_x = "EEG", modality_y = "EMG",                          channels_x = best[1, 1],                          channels_y = best[1, 2]) if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   plotCoherenceSpectrum(coh_detail) }

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: PhysioCrossModal provides tools analysing coupling, connectivity, synchrony physiological signals different modalities. single-modality analysis (e.g., EEG coherence channels) handled PhysioAnalysis, PhysioCrossModal focuses relationship distinct signal types – example, quantifying cortical EEG activity drives peripheral EMG motor task. package introduces: MultiPhysioExperiment – container holds multiple PhysioExperiment objects recorded simultaneously potentially different sampling rates. Spectral coupling – magnitude-squared coherence cross-spectral density modalities. Phase synchrony – Phase Locking Value (PLV), Phase Lag Index (PLI), weighted PLI (wPLI). Directed coupling – time-domain spectral Granger causality. Time-domain coupling – cross-correlation sliding-window cross-correlation. unified couplingAnalysis() wrapper dispatches methods single function call. vignette walks cortico-muscular coherence (CMC) analysis worked example – common paradigm motor neuroscience goal quantify functional coupling cortical EEG peripheral EMG sustained isometric contraction. References: Mima & Hallett (1999), Halliday et al. (1995).

what: Creating simulated EEG and EMG data
title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: real experiment import data PhysioCore::readEDF() similar /O functions. generate synthetic signals known 20 Hz coupling (beta-band CMC peak typically observed steady-force tasks). Note: real CMC research, coherence values typically range 0.1–0.4. use higher coupling strength pedagogical clarity. Additionally, real EMG data rectified (full-wave rectification) CMC analysis.
code: library(PhysioCrossModal) #> Loading required package: PhysioCore #> Warning: replacing previous import 'S4Arrays::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' by #> 'DelayedArray::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' when loading 'SummarizedExperiment'  set.seed(42)  # --- Parameters --- sr_eeg <- 500          # EEG sampling rate (Hz) sr_emg <- 1000         # EMG sampling rate (Hz) n_sec  <- 10           # recording duration (seconds) cmc_freq <- 20         # coupling frequency (Hz) cmc_strength <- 0.7    # coupling strength (0 = none, 1 = perfect)  n_eeg <- as.integer(sr_eeg * n_sec) n_emg <- as.integer(sr_emg * n_sec) t_eeg <- seq(0, by = 1 / sr_eeg, length.out = n_eeg) t_emg <- seq(0, by = 1 / sr_emg, length.out = n_emg)  # Shared 20 Hz oscillation (the "cortical drive") driver_eeg <- sin(2 * pi * cmc_freq * t_eeg) driver_emg <- sin(2 * pi * cmc_freq * t_emg)  # Four EEG channels -- only channel 1 carries the CMC signal n_eeg_ch <- 4 eeg_data <- matrix(rnorm(n_eeg * n_eeg_ch), nrow = n_eeg, ncol = n_eeg_ch) eeg_data[, 1] <- eeg_data[, 1] + cmc_strength * driver_eeg  # Two EMG channels -- only channel 1 carries the CMC signal n_emg_ch <- 2 emg_data <- matrix(rnorm(n_emg * n_emg_ch) * 0.5, nrow = n_emg, ncol = n_emg_ch) emg_data[, 1] <- emg_data[, 1] + cmc_strength * driver_emg

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: Granger causality (Granger 1969; Geweke 1982) quantifies directed coupling – tells whether past signal X helps predict future signal Y, beyond Y’s past can predict. particularly relevant CMC cortico-muscular drive thought predominantly (though exclusively) descending (EEG drives EMG). Note: Granger causality work correctly, signals must resampled rate. pass MultiPhysioExperiment, internal signal extraction handles automatically.
code:
gc_result <- grangerCausality(   mpe,   modality_x = "EEG",   modality_y = "EMG",   order      = 10L        # AR model order )  cat(sprintf("GC (EEG -> EMG) = %.4f
", gc_result$gc_xy)) #> GC (EEG -> EMG) = 0.0181 cat(sprintf("GC (EMG -> EEG) = %.4f
", gc_result$gc_yx)) #> GC (EMG -> EEG) = 0.0966 cat(sprintf("Net GC          = %.4f
", gc_result$net_gc)) #> Net GC          = -0.0784 # Positive net_gc indicates EEG drives EMG more than the reverse

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: PhysioCrossModal v0.2.0 provides two complementary approaches assessing statistical significance coupling estimates: surrogate-based null-hypothesis testing block-bootstrap confidence intervals.

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: surrogateTest() generates null distribution randomising phase spectrum (circularly shifting) one signal, thereby destroying cross-signal relationship preserving autocorrelation:
code: surr <- surrogateTest(   mpe,   modality_x = "EEG",   modality_y = "EMG",   method     = "coherence",   n_surrogates = 19,   nperseg = 256L ) cat(sprintf("Observed = %.3f, p = %.4f, 95%% threshold = %.3f\n",             surr$statistic, surr$p_value, surr$threshold_95)) #> Observed = 0.933, p = 0.5500, 95% threshold = 0.940

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: bootstrapCI() uses moving-block bootstrap (preserving temporal autocorrelation) construct confidence intervals:
code: boot <- bootstrapCI(   mpe,   modality_x = "EEG",   modality_y = "EMG",   method     = "coherence",   n_boot     = 19,   ci         = 0.95,   nperseg    = 256L ) cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.3f, %.3f]\n", boot$ci_lower, boot$ci_upper)) #> 95% CI: [0.828, 0.900]

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
text: Welch-based coherence gives single frequency-domain estimate averaged entire recording, wavelet coherence (waveletCoherence()) reveals time-frequency coupling dynamics. particularly useful coupling strength varies time (e.g. movement onset task transitions).
code: wcoh <- waveletCoherence(   mpe,   modality_x = "EEG",   modality_y = "EMG",   frequencies = seq(10, 35, by = 1),   n_cycles = 7,   smoothing_cycles = 3 ) # wcoh$coherence is a [time x frequency] matrix # wcoh$phase contains the phase differences # wcoh$coi contains the Cone of Influence frequencies  # Wavelet PLV is also available: wplv <- waveletPLV(   mpe,   modality_x = "EEG",   modality_y = "EMG",   frequencies = seq(10, 35, by = 1) )

title: Introduction to PhysioCrossModal
